app.tagline: Homelab dashboard with automatic network discovery
discovery.remoteOnlyBanner: Local scan disabled on NAS. Optional remote agent — see Settings → Automatic discovery.
discovery.remoteOnlyHint: Local scan disabled — optional remote agent on another LAN host (deploy/agent).
discovery.passiveIntro: Passive discovery — ARP table read every few minutes, no TCP scan (IPS/SEP friendly). Devices appear as host tiles; full service scan: use Scan network.
discovery.passiveWaiting: Passive ARP: first read in progress…
discovery.onDemandHint: On-demand discovery — use Scan network. No background scanning.
discovery.offHint: Discovery off — add services manually or run a manual scan.
discovery.adaptiveIntro: Automatic discovery — TCP in background (/28 chunks, network rotation). Live hosts are probed on ~190 service ports (gradually). Never scans a full /24 in one cycle.
discovery.adaptiveModeHint: Automatic discovery — low-priority TCP in background. Set CIDR networks in Automatic discovery tab. Manual scan: Settings → Scanning or Scan options.
discovery.tcpWaiting: TCP scan: first cycle in progress…
discovery.adaptiveWaiting: TCP scan: first cycle in progress…
discovery.arpModeHint: Automatic ARP discovery — devices detected from ARP table. Manual TCP scan: Settings → Scanning → Manual scan (advanced).
discovery.arpWaiting: ARP scan: first cycle in progress…
discovery.useAgentInstead: Manual /24 blocked (NETDASH_MANUAL_SCAN_ALLOW_FULL_CIDR=false). Pick a narrower network (e.g. /28) in Scan options, or allow full CIDR / disable safe mode.
discovery.useAgentInsteadBg: Manual /24 blocked (legacy safe-mode limit). Background discovery follows your policy — set CIDR in Settings → Automatic discovery.
discovery.autoIntro: QNAP scans LAN via ARP (arp-scan) — lightweight like WatchYourLAN. Remote agent optional when discovery runs elsewhere.
discovery.installHintOptional: Only when discovery should run from a machine other than QNAP. Not required when NetDash runs on your homelab server.
discovery.installHint: Optional on a host with LAN access — when QNAP is not the discovery server.

modal.scan.title: Network scan
modal.scan.descAdaptive: TCP discovery runs automatically in background (/28 chunks). Manual scan uses the CIDR you select (default from settings, typically /24).
modal.scan.descOnDemand: On-demand discovery — no background scan. Manual scan covers the full CIDR you select (default from settings, typically /24), with IPS-friendly throttling in safe mode.
modal.scan.adaptiveWarning: Automatic discovery scans in small background chunks. Manual /24 loads the network more — confirm if prompted; prefer /28 for careful scans.
modal.scan.safeModeWarning: Legacy safe mode: max /28 for manual scan. Full /24 disabled (NETDASH_MANUAL_SCAN_ALLOW_FULL_CIDR=false).
modal.scan.safeModeWarningBg: Legacy safe mode: max /28 for manual scan. Background discovery follows your policy (Settings → Automatic discovery).
modal.scan.safeModeThrottleWarning: Safe mode: IPS-friendly throttling (low parallelism). Manual scan may cover full /24 from settings — SEP note: prefer stealth delays; use /28 for a careful subset.
modal.scan.descManual: On-demand manual scan. Pick a CIDR — large networks require confirmation.
modal.scan.manualWideWarning: Scanning /24 or wider loads network and CPU. Prefer a narrower CIDR (/28) if hardware is weak, or keep IPS-friendly delays.
modal.scan.desc: Choose a network (CIDR) to scan or enter your own. On a weak NAS use a smaller mask, e.g. /28.

settings.aboutDescriptionPlaceholder: Short NetDash description shown on the About tab…
settings.aboutDescriptionHint: Shown on the About tab (read-only view).
settings.autoDiscoveryCidrHint: Background scan: network rotation, /28 chunks, port probes on live hosts only. One network per line or comma-separated.
settings.discoveryPolicyHint: On demand = Scan network button only. Passive = ARP table without TCP scan. Legacy adaptive = continuous background TCP (may trigger SEP).
settings.discoveryScheduleHint: UTC time (e.g. 03:00) or interval (e.g. 24h, 6h). One full cycle, then idle.
settings.discoveryLegacyWarning: Legacy adaptive scans continuously in background — may trigger IPS (Symantec SEP). Prefer On demand or Passive.
settings.discoveryEnvLocked: Locked by NETDASH_DISCOVERY_ENABLED / NETDASH_DISCOVERY_POLICY in .env — changes here have no effect.
settings.discoveryDisabledStatus: Automatic scanning disabled — manual service add only.
settings.manualScanIntro: Triggered via Scan options button. Has hard limits — does not replace background discovery.
settings.scanCidrHint: One network per line or comma-separated. Supports /24–/22 masks.
settings.dockerScanWarning: NetDash runs in Docker ({ip}, {network}) — this is the container network, not your LAN. Set NETDASH_SCAN_CIDR or CIDR in Settings → Scan (e.g. 192.168.1.0/24). In bridge mode map ports and set CIDR — see DEPLOYMENT.md.
scan.configWarning: LAN scan may not work — the container sees Docker network ({ip}, {network}), not your LAN. Set NETDASH_SCAN_CIDR=192.168.1.0/24 in Dockge or CIDR in Settings → Scan, then restart the container.
settings.scanProfile.heading: Scan profile
settings.scanProfile.safeDesc: Default — low parallelism, short port list, host cap. Recommended on every homelab; especially on weak servers.
settings.scanProfile.normalDesc: Faster scan (NETDASH_SCAN_SAFE_MODE=false). Use only on capable hardware.
settings.scanProfile.aggressiveDesc: Full port scan — heavy CPU and network load. May freeze weak hosts.
settings.scanProfile.weakHardwareHint: On weak hardware (RPi, old PC, NAS, N100) keep safe mode and a smaller CIDR (/28 instead of /24). To disable safe mode: NETDASH_SCAN_SAFE_MODE=false in compose + restart.
settings.scanProfile.confirmAggressive: Full scan by default loads the network and CPU (aggressive profile). On a weak NAS it may freeze the system. Continue?
settings.scanProfile.confirmFullScanSafe: Full scan is blocked in safe mode — this option applies only after NETDASH_SCAN_SAFE_MODE=false. Save anyway?
settings.scanProfile.safeFullScanNote: Full scan is disabled while NETDASH_SCAN_SAFE_MODE=true.
settings.hostPortsHint: Scanned in default mode alongside web ports
settings.hostOnly: Cards for hosts with no open ports (ping only)
settings.scanTest.readyFail: Scan not ready — set CIDR and verify compose (bridge + NETDASH_SCAN_CIDR).
settings.staleDaysHint: Removes auto-discovered services offline longer than this (excludes pinned and manual)

settings.solHelp.title: How to configure Sleep-on-LAN
settings.solHelp.intro: The 💤 button in NetDash sends a SOL magic packet to the host. For sleep to work, each target machine must run an agent listening on a UDP port (default 9).
settings.solHelp.gptwolHint: Alternatively, set a GPTWOL URL above — NetDash will send WoL/SOL via the gateway instead of locally.
settings.solHelp.linuxDesc: Install sleep-on-lan (pip or Docker). The agent listens on UDP and sleeps when it receives a packet with the reversed MAC.
settings.solHelp.linuxFirewall: Firewall: allow UDP port 9 (or another sol_port from NetDash settings).
settings.solHelp.windowsDesc: Use the sleep-on-lan Windows port, Depicus WakeOnLan tools, a custom PowerShell UDP listener, or another SOL agent. Run as a service (NSSM or Task Scheduler at startup).
settings.solHelp.windowsFirewall: Windows Firewall: inbound UDP rule for the chosen port (default 9).
settings.solHelp.macosDesc: Install sleep-on-lan or a custom UDP script. pmset handles local sleep, but SOL requires a persistent network listener on the host.
settings.solHelp.macosFirewall: System Settings → Network → Firewall: allow the SOL agent application.
modal.solHelpLink: How to enable SOL on the host?
settings.sol.scripts.title: SOL host install scripts
settings.sol.scripts.hint: Run the selected script on the target machine (as root / administrator). MAC is auto-detected — no manual entry needed. It listens on the SOL UDP port from NetDash settings and suspends the host when a reversed-MAC magic packet is received.
settings.sol.scripts.serviceHint: Script tailored to this service's MAC. Run it on the target host.
settings.sol.scripts.security: Requires administrator privileges. Firewall must allow UDP from the NetDash server subnet. Enable Wake-on-LAN in BIOS (for the ⚡ button).
service.sol.getScript: Get SOL install script for this service

about.updates.hint: Check the latest release on GitHub (requires internet). Auto-update needs docker-compose.full.yml, a :latest image tag (not a pinned semver), and a running netdash-watchtower container. Update now requires docker.sock on the host.
about.updates.applyUnavailable: A newer version is on GitHub, but in-app update needs NETDASH_UPDATE_APPLY_ENABLED and a mounted docker.sock (usually unavailable on QNAP). Use Watchtower or Pull in Dockge.
about.updates.applyWatchtower: Automatic update via Watchtower (every ~{hours} h) — nothing to do.

about.updates.modal.watchtowerFallbackBo: Dockge → Pull image → Restart container. In-app update needs docker.sock — unavailable on QNAP.

scan.noResults: Scan complete — no devices or services found on the given network.
scan.emptyHint: Last scan found nothing — check CIDR (e.g. 192.168.1.0/24) in Settings → Scanning and run scan again from the Services tab.
scan.emptyHintDocker: Container cannot reach LAN (Docker network) — set NETDASH_SCAN_CIDR in compose or Settings → Scan (see DEPLOYMENT.md).
scan.emptyHintPing: ICMP ping blocked — NetDash used TCP scan. Verify CIDR and cap_add: NET_RAW in compose.
scan.safeModeWarning: Legacy safe mode — manual scan max /28 (~16 hosts). Full /24 blocked. Discovery follows policy (default on-demand, no background TCP).
scan.safeModeThrottleWarning: Safe mode — IPS-friendly throttling. Manual “Scan network” covers the full CIDR from settings (typically /24), not only a /28 chunk. Discovery follows policy (default on-demand).
scan.qnapSafeWarning: QNAP / NAS: prefer /28 for careful scans. Container RAM limit does not protect against aggressive /24 — use Scan options…
scan.error.cidrTooWide: Range {cidr} is too wide for legacy safe mode (max /{max}). Use Scan options… and set e.g. 192.168.1.144/28, or set NETDASH_MANUAL_SCAN_ALLOW_FULL_CIDR=true.
scan.confirmWideCidr: Warning: /24 (or wider) loads the network and may trigger endpoint IPS (e.g. Symantec SEP). NetDash uses IPS-friendly delays — continue only if intentional.
scan.confirmLowResource: Network scan loads CPU and network (especially without ICMP — TCP sweep). Continue? On weak hardware use a smaller CIDR (/28) or scan off-peak.
scan.safeModeFullScanDisabled: Full scan disabled in safe mode — using quick port scan.
scan.error.sessionExpired: Session expired — log in again and start the scan.
scan.error.server: Server rejected the scan (error {status}). Check container logs.
scan.error.pollFailed: Lost connection to scan — check container logs and try again.
scan.error.pollRetry: Scan in progress — server not responding (attempt {n}/{max}). Waiting for container…
error.noConnection: Cannot connect to NetDash at this address. Check that the server is running (http://{host}:18787) — {detail}
error.networkFetch: Cannot reach NetDash (http://{host}:18787). Check the container in Dockge and refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R).
error.requestTimeout: Request timed out — server is not responding.
error.dashboardLoad: Failed to load dashboard: {detail}. Use http://{host}:18787 and refresh the page (Ctrl+Shift+R).
